thread:
ryan: Quick follow-up on the KV paging + attention kernel compatibility RFC — ran into an interop gap when eviction hits mid-generation. Short thread to capture options and owners.

marta: Ack. Can you paste the failing trace?

ryan: Sure — high level: generator requests tokens, kernel expects full contiguous KV prefix for cross-attention. Eviction removed a middle page; runtime tried to stream a page fetch which made kernel assert on contiguous kv length.

chao: Oof. That’s the classic assumption: many kernels assume monotonic KV layout (contig by layer/time).

elaine: Is this only for quantized kernels or for float kernels too?

ryan: Happens on both. Float kernels tolerate missing values less because the runtime had no interpolation path. Quantized ones sometimes masked them but produced bad attention.

sam: Options I see: 1) runtime ensures contiguity by pinning hot prefix pages during active generation; 2) kernel adds a non-contiguous KV read path (scatter-gather); 3) runtime provides a compacted view (linearize pages into a temporary buffer) as a shim.

marta: Tradeoffs: pinning increases memory footprint and reduces eviction efficacy. Kernel scatter-gather increases kernel complexity and might hurt throughput if it breaks vectorized memory layout. Temp buffer adds copy overhead per request but keeps kernel simple.

chao: Agree. Also consider fragmentation: repeated small evictions create a fragmented address space meaning the temp-copy cost grows with number of fragments, not tokens.

elaine: Could we make a hybrid: runtime maintains small per-stream coalescing window (merge adjacent pages into a single backing blob lazily) and only fall back to kernel scatter-gather for extremely fragmented cases?

sam: That seems reasonable. Need an interface so kernels can advertise support levels: e.g., kernel_capabilities = ["contig_only","scatter_gather","partial_fill_tolerant"]. Then runtime picks path at allocation time.

ryan: I propose adding a tiny Runtime->Kernel handshake on model load: KernelInfo.capabilities and KernelInfo.max_fragment_count and preferred_page_size. Runtime uses that to decide whether to pin/coalesce or convert.

marta: API shape looks fine. We should also define performance SLAs: e.g., coalescing copy must not exceed X ms for 99th percentile for short prefix lengths; otherwise fallback to kernel path. Needs benchmarks.

infra-bot: FYI: created perf-run job kv-paging-interop-2026-03-21, owner @sam.

sam: Thanks infra-bot. Action items I see: (A) implement KernelInfo capability enum + handshake (owner: chao). (B) implement runtime coalescer buffer with small LRU coalescing window (owner: sam). (C) add kernel shim path for scatter-gather (owner: marta). (D) perf harness and regression tests (owner: sam).

chao: For the coalescer: consider mitigating copy cost by reusing pinned GPU buffers and using async memcpy. Also maintain a per-stream "fragment map" so we can fast detect when copy vs scatter path should be used.

elaine: Also need correctness tests for partial-eviction during streaming generation; add a fuzz job that randomly evicts pages while a 1k token generation is active.

ryan: Good call. Also ensure audit logs show when a fallback path was used so we can correlate quality regressions to fragment events.

marta: One more nit: define what "fragment count" means precisely — number of discontiguous KV ranges across all layers? across single layer? Propose per-layer fragment_count and global_max_fragment threshold.

sam: Per-layer makes sense for kernel decision; runtime can aggregate for adaptive policies. Will add schema to RFC follow-up doc.

ryan: I’ll open a short RFC follow-up summarizing this thread and the action items. Please DM if you want different owners.

chao: I'll get started on KernelInfo patch.

marta: Adding unit tests for shim and a small perf microbench.

elaine: I’ll author the fuzz eviction test and add it to nightly.

sam: Plan: run infra job next Monday, report perf delta.

infra-bot: Job kv-paging-interop-2026-03-21 scheduled.

ryan: Thanks all. Closing loop when RFC PR has the handshake + runtime coalescer protos.
